channel.title: Learn :: FAU Cyber Security Club
channel.description: Every subject the club teaches, one section per stage of the roadmap.

item.title: Virtual Machines
item.description: Why virtual machines matter for security practice, how to set one up, and which hypervisor tools to use.

item.title: Linux
item.description: The Linux fundamentals security work is built on: filesystem, permissions, and processes.

item.title: Networking
item.description: IP addressing, protocols, and the tools used to inspect network traffic.

item.title: CLI & Scripting
item.description: Bash fundamentals and enough Python to automate real work from the terminal.

item.title: Web & System Fundamentals
item.description: How HTTP works and the system-level concepts behind most real-world vulnerabilities.

item.title: Windows & Active Directory
item.description: Why Windows and Active Directory matter for security work, and what this section covers.

item.title: Cryptography
item.description: What cryptography actually guarantees, why it matters even if you never write your own, and where it shows up in CTFs and real breaches.

item.title: AI
item.description: What language models and agents actually are, how agent systems are built, and why they are both a tool and a target.

item.title: Specializations
item.description: An overview of the security specializations to pick from once the basics are down.
